faq.a: Javed is associated with the Persian form جَاوِيد, whose core sense is javed; eternal, everlasting (persian).

faq.q: What is the origin of Javed?
faq.a: Javed is associated with Persian. Javed is Persian جاوید (jāvīd), meaning 'eternal, everlasting'. It is used as a male given name in South Asia and Iran.
No — the underlying form is Persian, not Arabic.
Javed can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Persian-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Javed should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Jāvīd is a Persian word, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.q: What does Javed mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Javed is rendered جاوید and carries the sense جاوید، ہمیشہ رہنے والا.

faq.q: What does Javed mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Javed is rendered جاوید and carries the sense جاوید، جاودان.
A romanized syllable approximation is ja-ved. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Javed?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Javed, javed. Script forms are جاويد, جاوید, جَاوِيد, जावेद.

faq.q: Is Javed a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
